rule: A name belongs here only when all three hold. (1) It is the proper name of a widely used technology, programming language, runtime, platform, operating system, vendor, product, protocol, standard, or file format. (2) A model has met it so often, in one meaning, that no project definition could make it less ambiguous. (3) It is not an ordinary English word or a general programming noun a project could give its own sense. A name that fails only (3), because its lowercase spelling is an ordinary word (Node, Chrome, Swift), goes under cased: only its capitalized spelling is skipped, and a lowercase use in a project sense stays a candidate. Never list a common word a project could give its own sense (hive, scope, core, run, session, store, owner, slice): that is where ambiguity lives, and such a word stays a candidate even written as a proper noun. Names are listed as written; matching under names ignores case and hyphens. The project's own name comes from its config and glossary, never from this file; a project adds names only it can vouch for under wellKnown in coherence.config.json. Bump version when an entry is added or removed.
